author: Han Li,Nayan Seth
description:
Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure has raised fresh questions about the future of US-China technology ties, as observers weigh the potential fallout from Washington’s policy on advanced AI chip exports to China.
The timing is particularly sensitive, with US lawmakers debating an annual defence authorisation bill amid growing calls to tighten restrictions on China’s access to advanced AI chips.
Ling Chen, an associate professor of political economy at Johns Hopkins University,...
title: Jensen Huang’s departure may signal tighter US controls on AI chip exports to China

author: Gabriel Dominguez,Caroline Lin
description:
Japan aims to become harder to defeat militarily and less vulnerable to economic pressure from China under plans to overhaul its three key security documents by the end of the year.
Analysts said the proposed revisions could make it more difficult for China to achieve its military objectives or use financial leverage on Japan, but that their impact would depend on Tokyo’s ability to translate its plans into practical capabilities.
Some also said that stronger Japanese defences could prompt...
title: As Japan looks to strengthen defences and security strategy, analysts warn of escalation

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Nvidia is searching for its first new leader in 33 years after Jensen Huang quit on Thursday, with interim chief Colette Kress, veteran engineers, members of Huang’s own family and the bosses of rival chipmakers all touted as possible successors.
The AI chip giant was left without the only leader it has ever had when Huang, 63, stepped down as president, chief executive and board member. The move was announced with immediate effect, according to a company filing with the US Securities and...
title: Nvidia’s hunt for Jensen Huang’s successor: insiders, rivals and a Trump pick

author: Igor Patrick
description:
The United States has paid to design a port infrastructure programme at Callao, the US State Department said on Thursday, as Peru moves its main naval base to expand the country’s busiest port, which rivals a Chinese-controlled megaport less than 80km up the coast at Chancay.
The US$4.5 million payment was disclosed in a note on a trip to Peru and Colombia earlier this month by Thomas DiNanno, State Department undersecretary for arms control and international security, whose remit includes...
title: US invests in Peru’s Callao as port battle with China’s Chancay megaport continues

author: Reuters
description:
Senior White House officials are discussing whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out amid a spy scandal surrounding Nvidia’s now-former CEO Jensen Huang, two people familiar with the situation said on Thursday.
A growing number of lawmakers criticised Lutnick for the administration’s refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government was properly overseeing Nvidia’s exports to China.
Criticism ‌of Lutnick’s actions...
title: White House discussing Howard Lutnick’s future as commerce secretary, sources say

author: Orange Wang,Eve Qiao,Alyssa Chen
description:
The United States and China should set up a dedicated hotline to help reduce the risk of AI-induced nuclear attacks, analysts have said.
The call came amid a fresh push by Washington to prioritise high-level talks on arms controls.
In a phone conversation on Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi agreed that meaningful leader-level conversations would help “advance goals such as peace and denuclearisation”, according to the Department of State.
US...
title: Cold War lessons for the AI age: how a US-China hotline could help stop a nuclear attack

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China on Thursday criticised Chile and Belgium’s combined bid to host the secretariat of the High Seas Treaty, accusing the countries of “politicising the bidding process and dividing members into opposing camps”.
The three countries had previously submitted competing proposals to host the secretariat – the administrative headquarters of the treaty, also known as the Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) agreement – until Chile and Belgium announced their joint bid on Friday.
Chile...
title: China slams Chile-Belgium bid to host High Seas Treaty body, pushes rival Xiamen proposal

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan will close its representative office in Papua New Guinea later this month after the Pacific island country repeatedly demanded its closure, citing its “one-China policy”.
The withdrawal will cut off Taiwanese technical assistance and end decades of cooperation with PNG, including halting spot-market purchases of the country’s liquefied natural gas (LNG) – a move Taipei said could deal a blow to the nation’s export earnings.
“It is deeply regrettable that, under pressure from [Beijing],...
title: Taiwan to close Papua New Guinea office and halt spot-market LNG purchases

author: William Zheng,Amber Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Thursday that Beijing was ready to engage in dialogue on Taiwan reunification with “people of vision” from across the island.
Xi pledged to accommodate the island’s realities but took a hard line against separatism in a speech at a ceremony marking the 160th anniversary of the birth of Sun Yat-sen, one of the nation’s revolutionary forefathers who is revered on both sides of the Taiwan Strait.
He said the reunification of the island with the mainland was an...
title: On Sun Yat-sen anniversary, Xi calls for dialogue on Taiwan with ‘people of vision’

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
The US confirmed the possibility of an unprecedented three-party presidential summit with Russia and China, as President Donald Trump prepares for an Asian tour next week.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio discussed the idea in a phone call with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Wednesday, according to the State Department. The meeting would take place alongside the Apec summit in Shenzhen, where Trump is already scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping.
Rubio and Wang “agreed on the...
title: Trump-Xi-Putin summit under discussion as US allies watch on

author: Alex Yu
description:
Nvidia boss Jensen Huang’s admission that he was unfaithful to his wife has become a widely discussed topic around the world, amid allegations linking the woman involved to Chinese intelligence.
While many social media users treated the affair as another piece of celebrity gossip, several Chinese professionals working at major Silicon Valley technology companies expressed concerns about its potential implications for their own careers.
If the billionaire founder of one of the United States’ most...
title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang affair revives China Initiative concerns in Silicon Valley

author: Ling Xin
description:
Hangzhou-based Star Vision will build Oman a network of 20 satellites that use AI to process images in orbit and spot ships and floods in real time, in what the company called China’s most valuable commercial space contract ever.
The deal – worth over US$200 million according to the start-up – was signed in Beijing last week with Omani firm Oman Lens during a landmark state visit by the country’s ruler, Sultan Haitham bin Tariq.
Besides the constellation, the package includes a satellite...
title: Silk Road in orbit: China to build 20-satellite ‘space AI’ system for Oman

author: Albee Zhang
description:
Taiwan will send Stan Shih, founder of computer giant Acer, to the Apec leaders’ summit in Shenzhen next week and has urged Beijing to ensure its delegation is treated with “dignity”.
Taiwan has been a member economy of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum under the name “Chinese Taipei” since 1991. But the self-ruled island’s leaders have traditionally not attended the summit due to political sensitivities and objections from Beijing. Instead, Taipei is usually represented by a business...
title: Taiwan to send Acer founder Stan Shih to Shenzhen Apec, calls for ‘equal footing’

author: Dannie Peng
description:
More than 20 Chinese start-ups are developing small modular reactors (SMRs) with ambitions to reshape the global energy landscape, according to the founder of one of the sector’s front runners.
Hu Po, founder of Weilan NuEnergy, a Shanghai-based start-up betting on the technology, noted that in 2024, as the artificial intelligence boom drove up energy demand, nuclear power – particularly SMRs – began to attract substantial capital in the United States.
Hu said that in China, the start-up teams...
title: China has more than 20 small nuclear reactor start-ups. Should the US worry?
